hints: Look first at the middle column. The pulmonary artery is unusual because it is an artery that leaves the heart to go to the lungs, so think about whether its blood is oxygenated or deoxygenated.

Now compare arteries with veins. Arteries need thicker, more muscular walls for higher pressure, but remember pulmonary pressure (to the nearby lungs) is much lower than systemic pressure (to the whole body).
walkthrough:
**Recall what the pulmonary artery does**

Think heart to lungs. The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood out in the pulmonary artery to pick up oxygen in the lungs. That one fact lets you cross out any row that says oxygenated.

**Use artery structure and pressure**

All arteries carry blood away from the heart under pressure, so they have much thicker walls than veins. Typical rule:
$$artery\ wall > vein\ wall$$
And pulmonary blood pressure is moderate, higher than in veins but much lower than in the aorta which drives blood around the whole body.

**Match to row A**

Row A has deoxygenated blood, a thick wall of $1.30\ mm$, and pressure of $15-30\ mmHg$. That fits an artery with lower pressure than the systemic circuit. Perfect match for the pulmonary artery.

options.A: Correct. Thick arterial wall, deoxygenated blood going to lungs, and moderate pressure of 15-30 mmHg fits the pulmonary artery.
options.B: This is the aorta, the main systemic artery. Very thick wall and very high pressure of 80-120 mmHg with oxygenated blood.
options.C: This is the pulmonary vein. Thin wall, low pressure, but oxygenated blood returning from lungs to the heart.
options.D: This is a systemic vein such as the vena cava. Thin wall, deoxygenated blood, and very low pressure of 3-8 mmHg.
